To execute, hand off to the relevant skill.

trending.name: karpathy-guidelines
trending.summary: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.

trending.name: agent-browser-debug
trending.summary: Experimental web app debugging through the agent-browser CLI - it opens pages, interacts by accessibility refs, and collects console, page errors, network, and screenshots as evidence. Local apps by default; a deployed one only on the owner's word. Use only when the user invokes /agent-browser-debug.

trending.name: received-review
trending.summary: Technical validation of review feedback before any fix. Use when code-review findings, PR comments, CI review output, or reviewer suggestions (human, subagent, GitHub, static analysis) need a verdict or disposition.

trending.name: session-learnings
trending.summary: Records lasting learnings from the session in the project's gitignored docs/session-learnings/AGENTS.md without asking, and on a separate request triages the notes into AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, global instructions, or a stronger enforcement such as a check or test, applying only approved edits. Use when pitfalls, user corrections, conventions, or commands that finally worked should reach future agents, whatever the conversation language, and when an installed agentflow chain calls it after finalize. Not for auditing instruction files (maintain-agents-md) or general memory and skill improvement requests.

trending.name: playwright-debug
trending.summary: Python Playwright testing of local web apps. Use when verifying frontend functionality, debugging UI behavior, capturing browser screenshots, or viewing browser console logs.

trending.name: request-review
trending.summary: Independent code review of an implementation against its requirements and the Git diff. Use when a completed or partially committed implementation, committed or in the working tree, needs that review.

trending.name: maintain-agents-md
trending.summary: Create, audit and maintain repository agent instructions and context architecture. Use when working on AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/, or instruction-related SKILL.md content - always-loaded context cost, stale, duplicated or conflicting instructions, agent memory drift. Not for human-facing docs or skill authoring (skill-crafting).

trending.name: tailwindcss
trending.summary: Tailwind CSS utility-first CSS framework. Use when styling web applications with utility classes, building responsive designs, or customizing design systems with theme variables.

trending.name: pricing
trending.summary: When the user wants to set pricing and packaging, or asks what to charge, whether to raise prices, or how to move existing customers: tiers, value metrics, per-seat vs usage, freemium and trials, willingness to pay, pricing pages. For in-app upgrade screens, see paywalls. For offers on services, courses, and high-ticket B2B, see offers.

trending.name: conversion-tracking
trending.summary: When the user wants to set up, audit, or fix conversion tracking to Google Ads, Meta, GA4, LinkedIn, and TikTok, or asks why conversions are missing or doubled: GTM, pixels, CAPI, Enhanced Conversions, offline imports. Fire on confirmed success, not the submit click; verify a test conversion arrives; diagnose before changing; offer free paths and disclose partner tools. For tracking plans, see analytics. For attribution, see attribution. For bidding, see ads.

trending.name: launch
trending.summary: When the user wants to plan a product or feature launch, or asks whether it's ready, when to announce, or how to get noticed: Product Hunt, beta and early access, waitlists, release go-to-market, launch checklists, release notes. For marketing after launch, see marketing-ideas. For the offer, see offers.

trending.name: schema
trending.summary: When the user wants to add, fix, or validate schema markup (JSON-LD), or asks which type fits a page or whether some markup is allowed: product, review, recipe, FAQ, rich result eligibility (FAQ no longer earns Google rich results), Search Console errors. For broader SEO, see seo-audit. For AI search, see ai-seo.

trending.name: image
trending.summary: When the user wants to create, generate, edit, or optimize marketing images, or asks which approach to take (generate, design, or photograph): blog heroes, social graphics, product mockups, banners, OG images. For ad images, see ad-creative. For video, see video.

trending.name: link-building
trending.summary: When the user wants backlinks and mentions that lift rankings and AI citations, or asks how to get sites to link or whether a link tactic is safe: link gaps, unlinked mentions, broken links, guest posts, best-of outreach. Never buy links that pass ranking credit: paid or exchanged placements get rel=sponsored or nofollow. For press, see public-relations. For directories, see directory-submissions. For reviews, see referrals. For communities, see community-marketing.

trending.name: free-tools
trending.summary: When the user wants to plan or build a free tool as marketing, or asks whether a tool idea is worth building or which one to pick: calculators, graders, generators, and other interactive tools for leads, SEO, and links. For downloadable lead magnets, see lead-magnets.

trending.name: ui-styling
trending.summary: Create beautiful, accessible user interfaces with shadcn/ui components (built on Radix UI + Tailwind), Tailwind CSS utility-first styling, and canvas-based visual designs. Use when building user interfaces, implementing design systems, creating responsive layouts, adding accessible components (dialogs, dropdowns, forms, tables), customizing themes and colors, implementing dark mode, generating visual designs and posters, or establishing consistent styling patterns across applications.

trending.name: marketing-loops
trending.summary: When the user wants a recurring marketing job an AI agent runs on a cadence or trigger, or asks what a weekly or daily automated check should do, remember, and when it should stop: SEO and ads checks, churn watches, outbound triage. For one-off ideas, see marketing-ideas. For the test loop, see ab-testing.

trending.name: revops
trending.summary: When the user wants to design revenue operations, or asks when a lead is ready for sales or why sales and marketing disagree on lead quality: lifecycle stages, MQL and SQL, scoring, routing, handoff, pipeline stages, CRM automation. For outbound copy, see cold-email. For email flows, see emails.

trending.name: marketing-ideas
trending.summary: When the user wants marketing ideas or growth tactics for a software product, or asks what to try to get attention or the next customers with little time or budget, or after the obvious channels. Draws on a library of 139 ideas. For a specific channel, see that skill (ads, social, emails, and others). For a full plan, see marketing-plan.

trending.name: reverse-engineer-marketing
trending.summary: When the user wants to know how another company grew and what to copy, or asks what a competitor did and when: a dated log of their moves against their traffic from public data, archives, job posts, reviews, and their funnel, compared with the user's data, ending in plays routed to other skills. Also finds where competitors are weak. For a snapshot profile, see competitor-profiling. For comparison pages, see competitors.

trending.name: events
trending.summary: When the user wants to plan, run, sponsor, or speak at events, or asks whether an event or booth is worth the money: webinars, conferences, booths, meetups, show-up rates, and follow-up into pipeline. For launches, see launch. For joint webinars, see co-marketing. For community programs, see community-marketing. For podcasts, see public-relations. For event emails, see emails.

trending.name: site-architecture
trending.summary: When the user wants to plan or restructure a website, or asks which pages they need or where something belongs: hierarchy, navigation, URL structure, internal linking, website builders and migrations. Not XML sitemaps (see seo-audit). For structured data, see schema.

trending.name: popups
trending.summary: When the user wants to create or improve popups, modals, slide-ins, sticky bars, and banners, or asks whether one will help or annoy and when to show it: exit intent, email capture, scroll and time triggers, announcements. For forms and pages outside popups, see cro.

trending.name: ab-testing
trending.summary: When the user wants to plan, run, or read A/B tests, or asks a judgement call on one: is the result real, can we stop, which version won, is this worth testing at all: sample size, duration, significance, hypotheses, and experiment backlogs. For tracking setup, see analytics. For page-level conversion fixes, see cro.

trending.name: paywalls
trending.summary: When the user wants to create or improve in-app paywalls and upgrade moments, or asks when or how hard to ask free users to pay (after they've seen value): upgrade screens, upsell modals, feature gates, limit-reached and trial-expired screens, mobile subscription paywalls. For public pricing pages, see cro. For pricing decisions, see pricing.

trending.name: cross-agent
trending.summary: Delegate a consultation, second opinion or installed-skill run to another agent CLI, keeping compatible sessions. Use when the user asks a different agent CLI for one of these. Review policy comes from an installed owner adapter.

trending.name: worktree-isolation
trending.summary: Safest workspace for development - work in place, an existing workspace, or a Git worktree. Use when deciding whether work needs isolation - before implementing plans, risky multi-file changes, parallel agent work, or clean-environment bug reproduction.

trending.name: implement
trending.summary: Task-by-task execution of an existing plan in the current session, with plan drift handling and verification. Use when executing a plan directly, including resuming interrupted execution. Not for subagent-driven execution (subagents-implement).

trending.name: frontend-craft
trending.summary: Subject-driven design and implementation of user-facing interfaces. Use when building, implementing, redesigning, reviewing, or refining pages, layouts, forms, navigation, dashboards, or reusable UI components in HTML, CSS, Vue, Nuxt, React, or other frontend frameworks, including implementation-framed changes to responsive design, styling, accessibility, visual hierarchy, interaction states, or user experience. Use alongside playwright-debug for browser verification (root-cause investigation of unexpected behavior is debugging).

trending.name: finalize
trending.summary: Integration or handoff decision for verified work, based on actual Git state and evidence. Use when verified work is ready for merging, pushing, opening a pull request, preserving or discarding a branch, or cleaning up its workspace.

trending.name: subagents-implement
trending.summary: Plan execution through coordinated subagents - delegation, review, verification, integration. Use when executing an existing plan via subagents, including resuming interrupted orchestration. Not for inline execution (implement) or unrelated parallel investigations.

trending.name: verify-gate
trending.summary: Evidence-backed pass or fail verdict on a completion claim. Use when work is about to be called done, fixed, ready, or mergeable, before a merge or pull request, a branch finish, or a handoff report.

trending.name: prose-craft
trending.summary: Edits prose to fit its reader. Use when drafting, rewriting, editing, or reviewing prose in any language for clarity, concision, tone, or audience fit (docs, messages, articles, product copy). Not for translation, agent instructions, UI design, dash audits (dashfix), negative-parallelism audits (negafix), or review findings (received-review).

trending.name: debug
trending.summary: Root-cause-first investigation of unexpected technical behavior. Use when investigating bugs, regressions, failing tests, build or integration failures, flaky behavior or performance anomalies.

trending.name: plan-craft
trending.summary: Multi-step implementation plan from an approved design or settled requirements. Use when a plan is needed before code changes.

trending.name: md-preview
trending.summary: Render saved Markdown, JSON, YAML, TOML, CSV or text files, including requests, specs and plans, as HTML previews with a table of contents, cross-file links, and a maintained folder README index. Use after an authoring workflow saves or edits a file, or when the user explicitly requests a preview. Not for arbitrary Markdown editing.
